newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council tries to draft Middle East resolution.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council tries to draft Middle East resolution.

text.p: The Security Council heard speeches all day Friday critical of Israel over the latest Middle East crisis but failed to agree on a resolution and decided to try again on Saturday.
Consultations were scheduled for 1500 EDT (1900 GMT), in hopes of being able to hold a formal meeting later to adopt a draft.

Almost all 50 speakers in the debate, requested by the Arab group, criticised Israel's new right-wing government in varying degrees for opening an archaeological tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem and accused it of delaying the Middle East peace process.

By contrast U.S. ambassador Madeleine Albright told the council: "Let us turn our attention not toward condemnation but toward encouraging the parties to restore the peace process and return to efforts to achieve concrete progress.

"Words here are no substitute for action in the region," she said, alluding to intensive U.S. efforts to arrange a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to end clashes which have claimed the lives of more than 50 Palestinians and over a dozen Israelis in the past three days.

The violence was sparked by the opening by Israel of a new entrance to an underground passage along the Western, or Wailing Wall, a Jewish holy place, which is near the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.
An Arab League statement accused Israel of opening the tunnel as part of a plot to destroy the Aqsa mosque and obliterate Islamic Arab landmarks.
Israel said the tunnel, intended as a window for tourists on 2,500 years of history, was closed on Friday but only temporarily.

A draft resolution proposed by the Security Council's non-aligned members, led by Egypt, would demand the complete closure of the tunnel and call on Israel to cease all acts affecting the safety of the Palestinian people.

It would also call for the immediate resumption of Middle East peace negotiations and the timely implementation of previously concluded agreements. Most speakers in the debate accused Israel of dragging its heels on both counts.
Diplomats said this draft was unacceptable to the United States, which has a veto in the council.

The non-aligned group was said to reject a blander version omitting any reference to the tunnel or criticism of Israel while calling for the cessation of all acts that might aggravate the situation and for an immediate resumption of peace negotiations and the timely implementation of existing accords.
